boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Loyola settings for solo work, group work, academic support, or a change of scenery.

cards.title: The Study
cards.subtitle: Jenkins Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Use the tables and chairs for a focused work session, then connect with tutoring or an organization consultant if your project needs support.
cards.short_summary: A Jenkins Hall study setting with quiet-study space and academic-support connections.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola lists The Study on the third floor of Jenkins Hall and describes tables, chairs, quiet study spaces, tutoring, and organization consultant appointments.
cards.source_title: Commuter Student Spaces | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Loyola identifies this as an open campus study space; confirm day-of access or service availability with the Thrive Center.

cards.title: Loyola/Notre Dame Library
cards.subtitle: East side of Loyola’s campus, between Loyola and Notre Dame campuses
cards.notes: Choose flexible seating for independent work, or use the library’s computers and research materials when your assignment needs campus resources.
cards.short_summary: The shared Loyola–Notre Dame library combines seating, computers, research materials, and study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola lists private and group study rooms, computers, research materials, a virtual gaming room, vending machines, and flexible seating at the Loyola/Notre Dame Library.
cards.source_title: Commuter Student Spaces | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: The library serves Loyola, Notre Dame of Maryland University, and the surrounding community; check current library access and room policies before arrival.

cards.entity_name: Loyola/Notre Dame Library Private Study Rooms
cards.title: Library Private Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Loyola/Notre Dame Library
cards.notes: Use a private room when you need a more contained work setting; verify current room availability and any reservation rules before settling in.
cards.short_summary: Private study rooms inside Loyola/Notre Dame Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola identifies private study rooms as an amenity of the Loyola/Notre Dame Library.
cards.source_title: Commuter Student Spaces | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Room eligibility, booking, and availability are not stated on this page; confirm current library procedures before relying on a room.

cards.entity_name: Loyola/Notre Dame Library Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Loyola/Notre Dame Library
cards.notes: Bring your group materials and use a dedicated group-study room; confirm whether a reservation or campus credential is currently required.
cards.short_summary: Group-study rooms at the shared Loyola/Notre Dame Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola identifies group study rooms as an amenity of the Loyola/Notre Dame Library.
cards.source_title: Commuter Student Spaces | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Room eligibility, booking, and availability are not stated on this page; confirm current library procedures before relying on a room.

cards.title: Fernandez Center
cards.subtitle: Evergreen campus
cards.notes: Use the building as an on-campus change of scene for coursework between classes; confirm which common areas are open when you arrive.
cards.short_summary: A named campus building Loyola includes among open study-space options.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola’s first-generation student FAQ lists the Fernandez Center among open study spaces where students can work between classes.
cards.source_title: FAQs | First-Generation Student Success | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Loyola lists the Fernandez Center as an open study-space option; specific room access is not stated.

cards.title: Study Rooms Outside Starbucks
cards.subtitle: Andrew White Student Center area
cards.notes: Check the rooms outside Starbucks for a separate place to spread out, then confirm current availability before beginning a longer session.
cards.short_summary: Named study rooms located outside Starbucks on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola’s first-generation student FAQ lists study rooms outside Starbucks among open study spaces where students can work between classes.
cards.source_title: FAQs | First-Generation Student Success | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Loyola lists these rooms as open study-space options; no reservation, eligibility, or hours details are provided on the cited page.

cards.title: Center for Intercultural Engagement Lounge
cards.subtitle: Andrew White Student Center, third floor
cards.notes: Use the lounge’s group-work space for collaborative coursework, and be mindful that it also hosts club meetings, conversations, and programming.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor Student Center lounge documented for group work and studying.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola describes the Center for Intercultural Engagement lounge on the third floor of the Andrew White Student Center as a space for group work and studying between classes.
cards.source_title: Campus Photo Gallery | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of the Andrew White Student Center; activities and programming may affect available lounge space.

cards.entity_name: Rev. Francis X. Knott, S.J., Humanities Center Porch
cards.title: Humanities Center Porch
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Loyola Quad
cards.notes: Bring a reading or laptop for an outdoor study break on the porch, and choose another indoor option if Baltimore weather is not cooperative.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Humanities Center porch Loyola specifically documents as a place to study.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola’s photo gallery describes the Rev. Francis X. Knott, S.J., Humanities Center porch as a place to sit, talk, study, and take in campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor setting adjacent to the Quad; availability depends on weather and any campus activity in the area.

cards.title: Academic Quadrangle
cards.subtitle: Evergreen campus
cards.notes: Set up on the central lawn for reading or quiet independent work when conditions allow, while leaving room for campus events and pedestrian traffic.
cards.short_summary: The central Evergreen-campus lawn, documented as a setting for study and contemplation.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola Magazine identifies the Academic Quadrangle as the central Evergreen-campus lawn and says quadrangles are intended for study, contemplation, socializing, and relaxation.
cards.source_title: Loyola Magazine, Fall 2024 | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: An outdoor central-campus lawn that also hosts clubs and annual events; weather and programming can affect its use.

cards.title: Writing Department Lounge
cards.subtitle: Maryland Hall, Room 038
cards.notes: Use this named Maryland Hall lounge for a focused academic stop, and confirm availability before planning around it because the cited page lists it for events.
cards.short_summary: A named lounge in Maryland Hall with an official room number.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola’s Center for the Humanities lists the Writing Department Lounge in Maryland Hall Room 038 as the location for a student grant information session.
cards.source_title: Student Grants and Funded Opportunities | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Located in Maryland Hall Room 038; the cited source documents scheduled use, not general drop-in access, so confirm access before visiting.
